questions.problem:
Determine the area $A$ of the parallelogram spanned by $\text{u}=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -1\end{aligned}]$ and $\text{v}=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 5\end{aligned}].$

$\,\,A=$ {{field-1}}
questions.worked_solution:
First, we construct a matrix where the columns are made up of the components of the corresponding vectors:

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}3 & -2 \\ -1 & 5\end{aligned}]
$$

Then, we find the determinant:

$$
\begin{aligned}det(M) & =|\begin{aligned}3 & -2 \\ -1 & 5\end{aligned}| \\  & =3\cdot 5-(-2)\cdot (-1) \\  & =15-2 \\  & =13\end{aligned}
$$

The absolute value of $det(M)$ gives the area $A$ of the parallelogram:

$$
A=|\,13\,|=13
$$

questions.worked_solution:
First, we construct a matrix where the columns are made up of the components of the corresponding vectors:

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}-\sqrt{7} & a \\ 5 & -10\end{aligned}]
$$

Then, we find the determinant:

$$
\begin{aligned}det(M) & =|\begin{aligned}-\sqrt{7} & a \\ 5 & -10\end{aligned}| \\  & =(-\sqrt{7})(-10)-a\cdot 5 \\  & =10\sqrt{7}-5a\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, setting the expression for the determinant equal to $0$ and solving for $a,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}10\sqrt{7}-5a & =0 \\ 5a & =10\sqrt{7} \\ a & =2\sqrt{7}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.worked_solution:
First, we construct a matrix where the columns are made up of the components of the corresponding vectors:

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}2\sqrt{2} & a \\ 3 & 6\end{aligned}]
$$

Then, we find the determinant:

$$
\begin{aligned}det(M) & =|\begin{aligned}2\sqrt{2} & a \\ 3 & 6\end{aligned}| \\  & =(2\sqrt{2})\cdot 6-a\cdot 3 \\  & =12\sqrt{2}-3a\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, setting the expression for the determinant equal to $0$ and solving for $a,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}12\sqrt{2}-3a & =0 \\ -3a & =-12\sqrt{2} \\ a & =4\sqrt{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Calculate the area of the parallelogram spanned by $\text{u}=⟨-2,3⟩$ and $\text{v}=⟨4,-6⟩.$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we construct a matrix where the columns are made up of the components of the corresponding vectors:

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}-2 & 4 \\ 3 & -6\end{aligned}]
$$

Then, we find the determinant:

$$
\begin{aligned}det(M) & =|\begin{aligned}-2 & 4 \\ 3 & -6\end{aligned}| \\  & =(-2)\cdot (-6)-4\cdot 3 \\  & =12-12 \\  & =0\end{aligned}
$$

The absolute value of $det(M)$ gives the area $A$ of the parallelogram:

$$
A=|\,0\,|=0

questions.worked_solution:
First, we construct a matrix where the columns are made up of the components of the corresponding vectors:

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}3\sqrt{2} & a \\ -\sqrt{5} & 10\end{aligned}]
$$

Then, we find the determinant:

$$
\begin{aligned}det(M) & =|\begin{aligned}3\sqrt{2} & a \\ -\sqrt{5} & 10\end{aligned}| \\  & =3\sqrt{2}\cdot 10-a\cdot (-\sqrt{5}) \\  & =30\sqrt{2}+a\sqrt{5}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, setting the expression for the determinant equal to $0$ and solving for $a,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}30\sqrt{2}+a\sqrt{5} & =0 \\ a\sqrt{5} & =-30\sqrt{2} \\ a & =-\frac{30\sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{5}} \\ a & =-\frac{30\sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{5}}\cdot \frac{\sqrt{5}}{\sqrt{5}} \\ a & =-\frac{30\sqrt{10}}{5} \\ a & =-6\sqrt{10}.\end{aligned}
$$
